_comment: Example routes. dispatch.mjs reads dispatcher/policy.json when it exists, otherwise this file. The models are the ones these routes were verified with; copy the file, set each model to one your CLI lists, and re-probe a route before you mark it ok. Placeholders: {model} {effort} {variant} {task} {root} {prompt}; any other {name} is rejected before spawn, and braces inside the prompt are left alone. The argv is passed as an array: the prompt never reaches a shell.

architect.note: Claude Code itself is the orchestrator; it does not dispatch to itself.

breadth.statusDetail: UNSAFE BY DESIGN: --dangerously-skip-permissions turns every approval off and agy is not confined to {root}. Read 'Permissions and sandboxing' in the README, run it only where that is acceptable (a disposable VM, container or user account), then set status to ok in your own policy.json
_notes: UNSAFE: --dangerously-skip-permissions disables every permission prompt. agy can then run any command, edit any file this user can, use the network and the browser, and push with your git credentials. --add-dir {root} adds the worktree to its workspace; it does not confine agy to it.
agy ignores the process cwd and works in its own scratch workspace: --add-dir {root} puts the worktree in its workspace.
Print mode times out after 5 minutes by default: --print-timeout lifts the cutoff.

Print mode ends the session whenever the model decides to wait on a long command (for example a full test suite started 'in the background'). Brief agy to run only the tests of the files it touched, and give it slices whose verification is file-local.
Error result shapes are source-derived, not captured: only a SUCCESS result has been observed.

UNSAFE: --auto approves every permission request with no prompt, and opencode has no OS sandbox. --dir {root} sets where it works, not what it can reach: it can run commands, write outside {root}, use the network and your git credentials. See 'Permissions and sandboxing' in the README.
--auto: a headless run cannot answer permission prompts; without it a prompt can stall or be denied silently.
--pure: no external plugins or MCP servers at startup.
--dir {root}: without it, a relative path in the prompt was written relative to $HOME, not to the cwd the dispatcher spawns opencode in.
--variant: reasoning effort is a provider variant, not a separate model id. Check `opencode models` for the ids your providers expose.
--title {task}: names the session, so a later dispatch on the same task can resume it.
A session error is written to stdout only, as {type:'error', ...}, with stderr empty; dispatch treats it as the CLI's own refusal evidence.
-C {root}: an explicit working dir instead of relying on the spawn cwd.
-s workspace-write: codex's own OS sandbox confines writes to {root}, whatever the global sandbox setting is. This is the only shipped route with a real sandbox.
-o: the final message also lands in a file you can read back cleanly.
codex may stop and ask a scope question instead of guessing (exit 0, no changes): answer it in the brief and re-dispatch.
Usage is read from `codex app-server` (account/rateLimits/read) before and after each run; reading it spends no model allowance.

easy.statusDetail: example route: probe it once and set status to ok
_notes: A cheaper codex route for small slices: constants, renames, formatting, doc sync.
Refused until its status is ok: a route is verified live before it is trusted.

UNSAFE: --disable-approval runs every tool with no prompt and --user-input-auto-resolve answers its questions for you. --workspace {root} roots policy-gated tools at the worktree; it is not a security boundary. See 'Permissions and sandboxing' in the README.
A launcher wrapper may inject --yolo before this argv, which also turns muse's OS sandbox off: then nothing confines it at all, a git worktree is not a sandbox. Check `ps` once.
--workspace {root}: roots policy-gated tools at the worktree (muse otherwise defaults to the cwd).
--user-input-auto-resolve: auto-cancels requests for user input in a headless run.
--no-foreign-personal-context: skips global personal instruction files; the repo AGENTS.md is the brief.
muse ignores a repo CLAUDE.md when AGENTS.md exists in the same directory.
stdin is closed by the dispatcher: a bare `muse` with an open stdin opens its TUI and hangs.
Terminal error shapes are source-derived, not captured: only run.terminal.completed has been observed.
